entities.summary:
The Schmalkaldic War was a pivotal 16th-century conflict of the Protestant Reformation in the Holy Roman Empire. It took place from 1546 to 1547, pitting Protestant princes against the Catholic Habsburgs. This war was a defining moment in the Reformation, shaping the course of European history and setting the stage for the Thirty Years' War. The war saw the Protestant Union, led by Philip of Hesse and Maurice of Saxony, clash with the Catholic League, backed by Charles V of the Holy Roman Empire.

The Schmalkaldic War was a complex struggle, marked by shifting alliances and bloody battles. The war began in 1546, when Charles V launched a surprise attack on Protestant territories. The Protestant Union responded with a series of military campaigns, but they were ultimately unable to stem the tide of the Catholic League's advance. The war ended in 1547, with the Treaty of Passau, which acknowledged Catholic dominance in the empire.

The Schmalkaldic War had far-reaching consequences, shaping the course of European politics and religion. It paved the way for the Thirty Years' War, which would ravage the continent and leave deep scars. The war also cemented the power of the Catholic Church in the Holy Roman Empire, setting back the Protestant Reformation.

As Philip of Hesse noted, 'The war has left us with nothing but a legacy of blood and ashes.' The Schmalkaldic War may have been a regional conflict, but its impact echoed across Europe, shaping the course of history for centuries to come.
